title: Release pipeline: tick and verdict: a release moves on as soon as its before-and-after look is in
why: #317 and #318 (2026-11-27) each waited an hour between their before look and staging. Two causes. First, releases_tick's cron line on live reads */24 (the live read of Scheduled tasks, 2026-11-27 05:50 UTC), while Scheduler::JOBS sets it every 10 minutes and the before-and-after check's design counts on that (handoffs/piece3-check.md §3: "releases_tick (every 10 minutes)"; research/launch-plan-jan1-2026-11-26.md, item 2). Second, the site's read of the verdict file (raw.githubusercontent.com) came back empty from :00 until the late re-ask at 60 minutes, though the file was on main from 05:07:26 (run 45942037912); the job logs nothing, so the wait didn't say why. The fix, as the session manager ruled (2026-11-27, its own release, not the Scheduler bundle): (a) releases_tick puts its own line to every 10 minutes once (BeforeAfter::tickLine, through Scheduler::change's '10min' preset); a later Change on Scheduled tasks is a person's and stays. (b) beforeafter.yml asks the site to move on right after it commits a verdict (/api/releases-pull.php, the same endpoint and manners as release-ping.yml), and that endpoint now also runs BeforeAfter::advance; one advance at a time (a lock). (c) the verdict is read through GitHub's contents API on main (DocsRepo::now, with the key; raw only when the API is away), and a release whose verdict isn't there 30 minutes after it was asked says so once on its card, naming the file. Backend only: nothing a visitor sees changes.

changes.what: A release waiting for its before-and-after look moves on within a minute or two of the look's verdict, instead of at the next run up to an hour later
Scheduled tasks: Releases runs every 10 minutes (it read */24)

A release with no verdict 30 minutes after its look was asked says so once on its card: "Waiting for its before look: no verdict file on main yet (site-audit/results/beforeafter/N.json), asked N minutes ago"

The note: none at 10 minutes, once past 30, on the card's line, nothing else moved. The lock: a second advance does nothing, then goes on, the lock let go. (b) the real releases-pull.php in its own process: ok, the release's line, the verdict read through the contents API and never raw, the release moved on from waiting; a second ping in the minute 429 too_soon as before.
